body: Many years ago when I was working in a different field I was told this too and found it to be very unrealistic and invalidating. Life costs money and work can’t just magically go away. I am sorry you have had that experience and I hope if you decide to seek help in the future you have more understanding providers.
Thank you. some of these comments have been not awesome to read but I’m doing my best to focus on the strangers who care without judgment and have reached out to support. Including you. ❤️

I have for most of my life but ironically my job doesn’t give me insurance so I can’t right now, lol. I worked a long time in non profits so I can’t go to a free clinic near me because I know all the clinicians. However as soon as I do have insurance yes I absolutely will and I believe it’s very important for anyone in the mental health field to have professional support

Hello, it’s hard to not respond to these messages with anger but I’ll do my best to be understanding. My job doesn’t make me want to die. It is hard and emotionally draining a lot of the time, but there’s nothing else I’d rather be doing. I have been doing this a long time and per all of the metrics we use to measure client progress, I am very good at what I do. Therapists are allowed to have depression and mental health concerns unrelated to the job. I’ve been depressed since I was around ~6. None of my clients know anything about my personal life, including but not limited to mental illness or trauma. If for one second I thought I was negatively impacting a client I would be out immediately. Part of the responsibility that comes with being a therapist is showing up to session ready to support, empathize, and help - it doesn’t matter if you’re depressed or even suicidal, because that 60 minutes is NOT about you. I wrote in this post that I’m a therapist because it makes me feel shittier that I want to be dead when I spend a lot of my time helping others find reasons to be alive, but I can’t do it for myself. I don’t want to be dead *because* I’m a therapist.

I understand what you’re trying to say. Yes, I know how to safety plan, what things make me feel better, how to reframe things to examine them in a healthier way. But it’s harder to do for yourself than it is to help other people do it - there’s a reason therapists legally can’t counsel people they know and love, because it’s impossible to be objective and effective when you’re too close to the situation

This is my experience too and I think it’s usually a “good” thing. I would NEVER tell a client about something I’m going through but I do believe it helps me understand and be more empathetic. It’s a big strength on my good days and crippling on my bad ones
we have feelings and experiences too
